note: The Education OS app's Build Status / Release Plan table — canonical here since v0.109.0 (prompt 7, the template diet close-out: this literal was 49.8 KB in apps/education-os/template.html; extracted once by hand and now round-tripped by tools/extract_fact_bases.py, injected in place by tools/build_education_os.py at the __CXFACT:buildStatus__ placeholder). Each row is [component, status, production step] for one dated release entry; the app's Build Status view renders this array verbatim.
entries: The hearing track, the vision boundary clips & the cohort tracker (v60): 24 hearing blocks authored around one line — "he ignores me" is a referral, not a discipline problem — because the child who does not turn, mishears, watches faces to guess or gets loud looks exactly like a child not listening, and is punished before anyone tests them; the blocks teach the conversion from write-up to referral and how to raise it with a colleague without accusing them, alongside noise exposure and protection (the pair with every trade track), why hearing changes week to week, quiet as a free resource, devices and batteries, Deaf culture and the difference between access and cure, and the classroom strategies sheet that helps the whole room while naming no child and no cause — under the hardest boundary of the four domains: nothing goes in an ear, ever, and no threshold or audiogram enters the platform; the vision boundary card is rendered as its own 20-second clip in all 21 languages, because its line genuinely differs from oral — the educator runs the room, the distance, the lighting and the queue, and the supervising professional reads every result including the ones that look obvious — with 14 drafted languages watermarked on screen and six community-authorship languages carrying the English placeholder with a notice, each clip hashed in its pack manifest; and the Cohort Tracker makes certification operable: five rungs per domain with the blocks each covers, twelve-month validity for introductory rungs and six months for those that run stations and train others, live current/due/lapsed status, re-observation recording, and a roster export — a staffing record holding educator names, rungs and dates only, with a lapsed educator permitted to attend and learn but not to run a station, teach or hand over a referral, since a lapsed educator working a station invalidates the pathway
Authored (v60); clips rendered and hashed; the tracker holds no learner, patient or health data by construction
Certified reviewers replace each draft watermark; nutrition remains template-only until its extra rules are authored with a dietitian

The vision track, the boundary clips & the partner-signature gate (v59): 24 vision blocks authored from the community health program template — from "eyes do a job" and asking for a seat change without embarrassment, through the distance chart explained and why only a professional reads it, refractive error taught without diagnosing anyone, eye safety across the trade tracks, the glasses that get lost and the school scheme that keeps a child seeing, to optics on a bench and standing up a screening program — where the screening half being the most established of the four domains makes the boundary sharper rather than softer: educators set the room, distance and queue, and a supervising professional reads every result including the ones that look obvious, with acuity values never entering the platform; the volunteer boundary card is now a standalone 20-second training clip rendered for real in all 21 instruction and family languages (63 frames of text and colour, no people, no mouths, no eyes) with per-script typography — Arabic and Urdu shaped and right-aligned, Bengali conjuncts, CJK and Ethiopic — each clip registered by SHA-256, every non-English clip watermarked DRAFT on screen, and the six community-authorship languages carrying the English placeholder with an on-screen notice rather than a machine translation; and the Referral Pathway & Partner Signature page makes the template's hardest invariant operable: seven steps with a named role on both sides, six conditions that make a pathway invalid rather than signed, the licensed half per domain, three signature blocks, and a generated printable document — with the rule on its face that no program opens until a named clinical partner has signed, because a program with nowhere to refer to is not a program, it is a leaflet
Authored (v59); clips rendered and hashed; the signature document is a template for local legal and clinical review
Certified reviewers replace each draft watermark; real signatures go on paper before any domain runs a session

OH-1 rendered, the consent pack, and the health-program template (v58): the OH-1 lesson "Two minutes, twice a day" is now a real 54-second 1,620-frame MP4 — cut points computed by opencut-classic's own rust/crates/time crate, frames composited from the manifest as toothbrush and tooth-row diagrams on a model with a two-minute timer ring and the full-screen boundary scene, caption and SYNTHETIC SAMPLE labels burned in, and no mouths or people in any frame — registered in the video-proof registry by SHA-256 beside the Spanish render; the screening-day consent pack ships as generated printable files in 22 languages × five documents (guardian consent, child assent read aloud, the volunteer boundary card, the referral slip, the counts-only tally) as A4-ready HTML and plain text with a machine-readable pack.json, every non-English document watermarked DRAFT for certified review and the six community-authorship languages carrying the English placeholder with a notice instead of a machine translation; and the Unspoken Smiles pattern is generalized into the community health program template — seven invariants that travel with every domain (name the teachable and licensed halves, refer and never conclude, counts only, consent plus assent, the learner becomes the teacher, a ladder to a real job, and no program without a named clinical partner), four domains mapped (oral built; vision, hearing and nutrition ready to author) with their scope splits, and a skeleton generator producing the block outline, deliverables, required partner and the five prerequisites before a single session runs — with an extra hard rule for nutrition (no weighing, no measuring, no individual dietary advice, nothing that ranks bodies) and the hearing emphasis that what looks like inattention is often audiology
Authored (v58); the render is real; consent documents are drafts for local legal and clinical review
Certified translators replace each draft watermark; a named clinical partner signs before any domain runs a session

The oral-health & peer-educator track (v57): a 24-block preventive dental track from K-2 to adult — brushing and the sugar clock, why teeth hurt, fluoride read off a real label, the screening day, teaching a smaller child, access barriers mapped honestly, the referral script, the green-clinic audit, campaign design that measures without collecting health data, consent and child assent, training the next cohort, the numbers a program may keep, careers with named schools and licensing, infection-control principles from the outside, the community survey, standing up a program, and the fellowship bridge — sitting outside the 333,333 ledger like the government-training modules, so every arithmetic elsewhere is unchanged. One boundary is taught before anything else and carried as a scene in every generated lesson: peer educators teach prevention and hand over a referral; they never diagnose, treat, or put an instrument in another person's mouth, and every clinical act is named as a licensed one. The data rule is equally hard — screening days count people and never record health facts, no mouth photographs, no names against findings, no PHI in any tenant, the referral slip on paper with the family. Eight organization tools ship for programs like the one modeled: screening-day planner with consent packs and boundary cards, the Tier 0 printable curriculum, a cohort tracker that holds educators and never patients, a counts-only program dashboard, the consent and boundary kit, a clinic partnership template with a named role at every step, the fellowship portfolio builder, and the green-clinic audit with trade-offs named rather than greenwashed. The model is Unspoken Smiles as published by founder Jean Paul Laurent on MIT Solve and their own site — reviewed from the public record, quoted and attributed line by line, with no affiliation, endorsement or contact claimed and no impact number invented where they publish none — generalized into six design moves another organization can copy without touching anyone's brand or clinical practice, plus a lesson-pack generator (24 blocks x 21 languages) in which no frame shows a mouth
Authored (v57); every figure about the modeled organization is quoted from its own public pages and attributed
Local health authorities review the scope card per jurisdiction; a named clinic partner signs the referral pathway before any real screening day

The country brief, the Amity intro film & the adoption harness (v56): the landing page now carries the countries — a 44-country stat tile, a Global Editions flagship tile, a partner-countries link on the edition strip and a section head that names both registers; the Global Editions page gains the country one-pager generator: pick any of the 44 and it composes a ministry-ready brief — what that country receives, the seven amity commitments, its languages with each one's honest tier status (full instruction / family & caption / global partner shipping empty), the six-stage charter path from the ask through Tier-0-first printing and local language authorship to in-country conformance, and an explicit refusals list ending with the rule that no statistics about the country appear, because the platform publishes what it would do rather than estimates of a need the ministry has not verified — copyable as plain text that prints on one side of paper; the Amity Program intro film is storyboarded at 96 seconds around the paper-first story, and what it refuses is part of the design: no country footage, no flags, no borders drawn, no people in any frame — the paper, the documents and the empty rooms carry it, because a film about a program that has not deployed anywhere should not look like one that has; and the adoption harness ships as code in the foundation's OpenCut fork beside the plugin scaffold — tools/cogx-eval, dependency-free and air-gap runnable, with five fail-closed gates that have no override parameter anywhere (OSI self-hostable license, self-hosting, synthetic fixtures only, human gate preserved, landmark compatibility), a published weighted score reachable only after every gate passes, stub adapters whose scores print "this score measures the harness, not the model", and eight passing unit tests covering the refusals
Authored (v56); harness tests 8/8 green; zero deployments and the brief says so
A ministry or NGO ask starts the first charter; real adapters replace the stubs before any Treasurer verdict

Global Editions, 66 languages & the Maitrix review (v55): the Amity Program publishes a designed edition path for all 43 countries on the active UN least-developed-countries register (Sub-Saharan Africa 32, Asia 8, Pacific 3, Caribbean 1 — listed with their major languages, the register named and dated, graduation churn acknowledged) under seven sovereignty-first principles — ministry-chartered, in-country data residency as a landmark, paper-first Tier 0 as the first deliverable, local certifiers or an honest none, local language authorship on the Diné bizaad rule, free forever by the published funding commitments, and landmarks identical at every border — with the GPE/ECW/UNICEF/UNESCO frameworks described for fit, no partnership claimed and the deployment count published as zero; the language system grows 21 → 66 with the global-partner tier: 45 languages enumerated by region and script direction that ship deliberately empty — no machine drafts at this tier, promotion only by completed local review — and the conformance check becomes Languages = 66; and the requested Maitrix review lands in the Observatory: two entities distinguished honestly (the maitrix.io commercial model hub — not adopted, as a many-vendor hub contradicts the Treasurer's district-hosted policy; the Maitrix.org open research org — five Apache-2.0/MIT candidates mapped: llm-reasoners for LPAA/RTA, PromptAgent for the teacher-reviewed Advisor corpus, MIT Voila as the district-hosted voice candidate now on the upgrade waitlist, Pandora for twin simulation research, de-arena for federation-scale evaluation), all behind the standing gates with no contact made
Authored (v55); the LDC list is dated and verifiable; all reviews from public pages at review time
A ministry or NGO charter starts the first Amity deployment; any Maitrix.org adoption passes Treasurer + board and lands in the minutes

Onboarding 2.0, the edition comparator & ten capstone showcases (v54): the sign-in/try-free flow gets the front door's design pass — a gradient onboarding hero ("Two minutes from here to your first mission"), a three-step strip (say who you are → sign in or skip → land in your Today), role pills that set the home screen and tour, restyled provider cards, and every existing honesty note kept (the demo session is local, labeled, and under-13 sign-in is school-only); the Block Library wires into the Autopilot: any base block × any demo learner run under Foundation (F9) and Accelerated (A9) policies side by side — opening D, missions with re-teach and enrichment counts, weeks to seal, the flow/anxiety/boredom split, closing λ — with the reading rule printed (neither column is better; the right edition is the one whose flow row is fattest; same transfer check either way); and ten capstone showcase videos storyboarded through the media pipeline (The Working Coast, The Grid, The Ledger, The Cell That Builds, The Gated Swarm, The Cold Aisle, Signed Off, The Testimony, The Bridge Held, The Teach-Back) — 88 seconds each with the no-people-on-camera rule absolute in every scene (venues shown empty, minors never filmed), all-21-language caption plans, per-showcase and all-ten JSONL copy
Authored (v54); the comparator is a labeled synthetic simulation using the published edition parameters
Wave 1 replaces the sim with real cohort telemetry; showcases render when the first capstone night is booked

Landing 2.0 & the 3,333 Block Library (v53): the front door rebuilt as a modern, fast interface — a cinematic hero over the national art with a gradient display headline and three clear calls, an animated stat band (the 333,333 counter counts up; reduced-motion renders instantly), six "choose your door" role cards with drawn glyphs and guided-tour hooks, a synthetic-labeled activity ticker, an eight-tile flagship grid, the 56-edition flag strip and an honesty band — every fact and label unchanged, scroll-reveal and hover motion fully disabled under prefers-reduced-motion, keyboard access on every tile; and the Block Library: the 333 mastery blocks each published in ten teaching editions — Foundation/Standard/Accelerated intensities × nine-week/split-2×4.5 (the Summer Bridge form)/extended-12 pacings + the crew/co-teach edition — plus three statewide capstones (The Working Coast, The Grid, The Ledger): 333 × 10 + 3 = 3,333, verified by a new platform conformance check. Every edition publishes what the teacher runs, what the engine changes (opening band, thresholds, re-teach budget) and its automation policy; the transfer check and credential are identical in all ten — the ramp moves, the bar never does; LPAA proposes an edition per learner and the teacher's choice always wins. Browsable per block in the Course Builder with a JSON export
Authored (v53); the library is generated arithmetic over the authored blocks, and says so
Wave 1 teachers pick editions per cohort; capstone pilots need real audiences booked

The Civic Compass, app-store packaging & open agent interop (v52): a national civic-and-leadership dashboard at four altitudes — sorted comparison charts of the published NAEP/graduation/per-pupil series with the selected edition highlighted, the seven federal milestones, a five-rung leadership ladder, fifty-six state pages pairing the durable leadership facts (chief, board, LEAs, official links, named policies — officeholder names always verified at the source, never shown stale) with each state's leadership history as an exemplar timeline, and a district arena; place-based by user choice with no geolocation anywhere, and framed on-page as a tribute to the leadership and foundational example of Willie L. Brown Jr. — expressly not his program. Interoperability and scale: the app-store plan (installable PWA, iOS/Android from one codebase, kids-category rules — no ads, no tracking, parent gates; MDM for districts; a store listing that oversells is a conformance failure) with the cogx-module-package/0.1 signed-package spec that lets editions, tracks and language packs move between states with provenance and re-checked arithmetic; a tamper-evident video-proof registry (the ES proof render registered by SHA-256); and the open agent-economy interop design — Virtuals (GAME/ACP) and SingularityNET (marketplace/MeTTa) reviewed and mapped to the lodge's edge behind five non-negotiable gates, with a four-module adult elective including the failure modes
Authored (v52); charts from published data; interop reviewed, not deployed; no tokens held anywhere
Store builds follow Wave 1; the first marketplace listing, if ever, passes Treasurer + board + counsel

The family home's Thursday-signal preview now speaks all 21 languages: a two-tier selector (11 full instruction, 10 family & caption), family-tier signals rendered from their drafted templates with RTL support for Urdu, the draft watermark shown until certified review, and the Diné bizaad card carrying its English placeholder with the community-authorship notice. And the pack builder scales to whole tracks: any Future-Work track, every band, every block × 21 languages built in one click with per-band counts and JSONL copy — the Robotics & Automation pack ships as a zip alongside this release
Authored (v51); the render is real, the voice track is silent by design (TTS runs at the district tenant)
A certified translation replaces each draft watermark; the interactive classic import is the next proof step

The Media Studio gains the 21-language content-pack builder (one complete block → 21 render manifests, tiered and statused, downloadable as a pack) and the ten ED regional academy intro videos storyboarded through the same pipeline — 78 seconds each, built from each region's own published economy, anchors and tracks, English voice with all 21 caption tracks planned, no people on camera, synthetic labels surviving the edit. The plugins/cogx scaffold lands in the foundation's OpenCut fork as a reviewed proposal branch: manifest, JSON Schema for cogx-render-manifest/0.1, a dependency-free Rust crate skeleton with the six component traits (captions track renamed cogx.captions21), and a README that defers to upstream's architecture — ready for the day contributions open

Certified reviewers per language; the pack renders on a real headless build; the branch goes upstream when the door opens

Media Studio on the OpenCut fork (v49): the foundation's repo (AGIFutureFoundation/OpenCut, MIT, fork of OpenCut-app/OpenCut) reviewed at clone depth and integrated as the platform's video layer — six capability integrations mapping the upstream rewrite's own roadmap (Editor API → mission player embeds; plugin-first → the six-component G2FC plugin with retrieval markers, rubric overlay, twenty-one caption tracks, voice refs, metadata sidecar and a privacy lint that fails the export rather than the rule; one Rust codebase → every tier's devices; MCP server → driven through the lodge's bus by MRA, a new apprentice-tier Media Render Agent that decides nothing creative; headless mode → the per-tenant render farm where twenty-one languages are one manifest; scripting → steward automations in the minutes); five content pipelines (mission videos, family recaps, evidence clips under sight-sense rules, board briefings, the maker mode's embedded editor) under one standing rule — minors never on camera, no classroom surveillance, AI media labeled in frame, district-tenant rendering; and a working manifest generator: any real module → cogx-render-manifest/0.1 with storyboard preview, draft-caption status and retrieval markers, copyable as JSON

G2FC plugin stages in the fork; offered upstream under MIT when contributions open; embedded editor on the upgrade waitlist

The Lodge architecture & the Agent Observatory (v48): the agent flow is rebuilt on the organizational geometry of the Masonic lodge — used strictly as a reference metaphor from the public record, no affiliation implied — three degrees as agent tiers (apprentice executors propose, fellowcraft coordinators verify, masters audit; humans alone seal), nine officer stations mapped to the eight agents plus a Treasurer compute-ledger function, eight working tools as engineering disciplines (the gavel is model distillation, the square is conformance, the plumb is the honesty labels, the compasses are least-privilege), the two pillars, the human keystone, a seven-step optimized flow (tyled ingress, deacon batching, two-warden gating, keystone, signed minutes, budgeted compute) and a charter-and-recognition federation model for global scalability with six invariant landmarks; rendered in a new Observatory module with a tracing-board SVG, the full architecture tables and a Rosling/Gapminder-style motion chart — every agent a live color bubble (workload across on a log axis, human acceptance of proposals up, model size as area from the Treasurer's ledger), 2026–2033 time slider with play, trails, toggleable Voronoi territory cells, hover tooltips, a table view, and a per-year story line — categorical palette validated for CVD separation and both themes, everything labeled SYNTHETIC MODEL OUTPUT
Authored (v48); palette validator passing both modes; sizing illustrative, not benchmarks
Wave 1 minutes replace the synthetic series; the full-3D WebGL observatory joins the upgrade waitlist

The Integrated Practicum & eight-module guides for every audience (v47): the training system gains a Practicum tab — 24 hands-on missions across the six audiences, each done inside the live modules (run the Track Autopilot, generate your DPA rider, read a Student 360, draft the employer compact, face the clause 11 decision) with honest on-device verification: "verified" means this browser saw the state change, and nothing is reported anywhere; progress chips per audience, deep links into every target module, and a cross-link to the Guide's role tours for people who want the walk-through before the work. The four newer guides (students, school leaders, district offices, employers/partners) grow from six modules to eight, the new modules integrating v45–46 systems — the nine serving modes, owning verifiable evidence, rolling out agent senses, the Board 360 story, the clause 11 decision, conformance as a cadence, the contributor dividend, and verify-don't-trust credential checks — every scenario keeping the learn/try/coaching-reveal loop

Wave 1 steward sessions adopt the practicum as the institute pre-work
